answer: Proof of spacetime extends a one-time storage check across a long window, requiring the prover to answer repeated random audits while the data stays on disk the whole time. A raven circling a reef cannot fake continuous presence by fetching the file at the last second, and an atlas of audit timestamps shows gaps where the data was absent. A Sybil farm would have to keep every claimed replica resident for the entire period, so spinning up thousands of fake identities multiplies real disk and time costs instead of hiding them.
